title: Six-class (negation + GLV) parallel Pollard rho on secp256k1 with a global work meter and itemised step accounting (derived from 189ebc42)

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production secp256k1 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (six-class negation+GLV parallel Pollard rho: twisted R=8192 adding walk on classes keyed by |y|, exact 4-limb truncated canonical-index rule with metered fallback, doubling escapes from detected 2-cycles and checkpoint cycles of length <= 64, distinguished classes routed to 2^16 storage nodes each natively addressable below 2^56 bytes, re-walk solving) halts on every run after at most the exact integer W = 168908606169243874770580353093127547782800 milli-units (one unit = one batched incomplete affine secp256k1 addition, C=1000, and the meter counts milli-units, 1000 to a unit) because a global work meter charges every action before it runs and halts the run at W. The total is the ledger of proof.md section 5, three rows in exact integer milli-units: phase 1 168179125105034817391573251275519385410700 = 1150*(S_int + 2^60) with S_int = ceil(S_ops) = 146242717482638971643693383952366531642 exact; hard extras 232117299799551615389286625019528, below 2^97.56 units, every row of the section's table plus node set-up; and the Markov allowance 729480832091757579455486428321537352572 = ceil(random/0.0035), where the expected random extras are 2553182912321151528094202499125380734 and the allowance replaces them rather than being added to them, since it is their quotient by the 0.0035 the success statement subtracts. The three rows sum to W = 2^126.989510 units, so the claim 126.99 = 12699/100 is that total's ceiling at two decimals, certified by W^100 < 1000^100*2^12699 together with W^100 > 1000^100*2^12698, both 4,123-digit sides printed in certificate.txt. The ordinary step is charged 1.15 units (the reference addition plus a 150-instruction budget over 147 itemised instructions, with field inversion I < 2^17 from M <= 227). It succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed heuristic H1 (random mapping on N=(r-1)/6 classes with Brent-Pollard correction and a 5% slowdown allowance; partition, distinguished and routing bits pseudo-random), supported by toy runs; the meter's early-halt probability is below 0.0035 by Markov, so success >= 0.3914. Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing <= 2^59.0 units, enforced and included; no nonuniform advice. Construction credited to submissions 189ebc42 and 1c600df4 (declared dependencies). Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of every identity the walk uses and of the truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: the complete per-trail algorithm on prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3+7 (T_c census, pipeline success with node routing, long-trail trap test).
